entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Titus Geganius Macerinus was a Roman politician who served as consul in 492 BC with Publius Minucius Augurinus.

    Macerinus was born into a prominent patrician family in Rome and received a traditional education in Greek and Roman literature, law, and politics.

    As consul, Macerinus worked closely with his co-consul, Minucius, to pass laws that aimed to reduce debt and promote economic growth in Rome.

    Macerinus's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the success and the struggles of the Roman Republic during its late classical period.

    In the words of the Roman historian Tacitus, 'Macerinus was a man of great integrity and a just and fair judge,' who 'always put the interests of the people above his own.'
